messages:
sasha: Heads-up — PM asked for a single dashboard that shows cache effectiveness across runtime and infra. Need inputs for metrics and labels we can rely on. thinking: hit_rate, eviction_count, reuse_by_workload. who owns ingestion?
jonathan: I can expose runtime counters. plan to emit prom metrics from the serving process: `redwood_runtime_cache_hits_total`, `redwood_runtime_cache_misses_total`, `redwood_runtime_cache_evictions_total`, and `redwood_runtime_cache_prefix_reuse_total` with labels `model`, `route`, `tenant`, `seq_len_bucket`.
anya: Infra will pull those in via prometheus federation + pushgateway for hosted. We need cardinality limits — `tenant` and `route` can explode if not normalized. Can we standardize a `route_id` and cap `seq_len_bucket` to something like [<=32,33-128,129-512,>512]?
tyler: Console wants per-route and per-model slices plus a tenant-aggregate view. Also want derived metrics: `cache_hit_rate = hits / (hits+misses)` and `eviction_rate = evictions / requests`. Dashboard panels prefer precomputed ratios to avoid heavy client-side joins.
maria: Cost note — high-cardinality label churn in prometheus is expensive. If we keep `tenant` for enterprise only and use `team` for internal customers that reduces series. Also suggest sampling for low-traffic routes.
sasha: sounds good. jonathan, can runtime emit both raw counters and a lightweight `cache_hit_rate` gauge (5s scrape) so infra can avoid heavy queries?
jonathan: yes, runtime can export a `redwood_runtime_cache_hit_rate{model,route_id,seq_len_bucket}` gauge updated by a sliding window. We'll keep raw counters too.
leah: UX asks — provide consistent human-readable `route_name` in addition to `route_id` so product owners can interpret dashboard panels. But route_name must be non-unique and not used for cardinality.
anya: infra will add a relabel_config to drop `route_name` in Prometheus ingestion for cardinality, but we can store it as a label in long-term TSDB (clickhouse) for dashboards. Need the exact label name. propose `route_name_v1`.
sasha: good compromise. jonathan — can you include `route_name_v1` but flagged as high-cardinality so infra knows to strip? Example metrics snippet below:
```
# TYPE redwood_runtime_cache_hits_total counter
redwood_runtime_cache_hits_total{model="gpt-small",route_id="r-123",route_name_v1="chat-widget-v2",tenant="acme",seq_len_bucket="33-128"} 4523
```
jonathan: yes, we'll emit that. infra-bot: prometheus/alertmanager config change merged in staging: `reduce_cardinality_rules` applied.
infra-bot: federation job `cache-metrics-federate` scheduled every 30s for hosted clusters.
maria: For alerts, suggest `eviction_rate` > 0.05 sustained for 5m triggers paging, and `cache_hit_rate` < 0.6 for high-traffic routes triggers SRE page. Keep thresholds configurable per-tenant.
tyler: For dashboard UX, will add a toggle to switch between `per-route` and `tenant-aggregate`. Also need a table showing top 10 routes by eviction_count and top 10 by wasted_cache_misses. Can infra provide a pre-aggregated table endpoint?
anya: we can add a daily rollup job that writes top-N per cluster to ClickHouse. endpoint: `/api/telemetry/cache/top_routes` with `cluster` and `window` params.
sasha: action items recap: jonathan -> instrument metrics and include `route_id`, `route_name_v1`, `model`, `seq_len_bucket`; anya -> relabel rules + federate + rollup job; tyler -> dashboard wireframes and panels list; maria -> alert thresholds and runbook draft; leah -> product-friendly route naming guidance. I'll assemble a spec doc after this thread. cc @tyler @jonathan :thumbsup:
jonathan: 👍 adding instrumentation PR to draft today.
tyler: will post wireframes by EOD tomorrow.
leah: I'll share naming conventions doc.
maria: i'll kick off runbook draft and link it here.
sasha: thanks all — tagging this as `#telemetry` and `#dashboard` for search.
